title: Kota NEET-prep brand cut CAC ₹2,180 → ₹720 by swapping 'AIR 47!' boasts for 14 QR-verifiable rank cards
content: SITUATION: A Kota-based NEET/JEE prep app (tier-2/3 audience, ₹9,999 annual plan) spent ₹9.6L/month on Meta and Google but was stuck at ₹2,180 CAC — roughly 440 paid enrolments a month. The bottleneck was credibility, not reach: ad copy screamed 'AIR 47!' over stock-photo toppers, and parents in Patna, Indore and Nagpur flatly didn't believe it. Demo-to-paid sat at 6%, and of 600 coded YouTube/Instagram comments, 41% were variants of 'sab fake hai' and 'paid actor hoga'. ACTION: We stopped claiming and started proving. We filmed 14 actual 2025 students on their own phones at home holding their NTA scorecards, each naming a real mock-test arc ('412 to 658 in 5 months'). Each became a 40-second vertical Hindi reel plus a WhatsApp-forwardable PDF rank card with a verification QR linking to the public NTA result. We ran these as Meta/Instagram results-proof creatives and YouTube pre-roll, and retargeted demo drop-offs on WhatsApp with the one clip nearest their target score. OUTCOME: Over 11 weeks demo-to-paid rose 6% → 16.5%, CAC fell ₹2,180 → ₹720, and forwarded rank cards drove 2,400 organic referral demos (~390 of which converted). At near-flat ₹9.7L spend, monthly paid enrolments climbed 440 → 1,290.
lesson: In outcome-driven categories, an unverifiable boast reads as a lie to skeptical tier-2/3 buyers — and the louder the claim ('AIR 47!'), the faster they discount it. Don't polish the claim; make it checkable. Replace topper boasts with raw, named, QR-verifiable proof the buyer can forward on WhatsApp himself. Believability, not production value, is what converts — and a forwardable proof asset turns every skeptic into a distribution channel.
